content.thinking:
I'm designing a frost-forged battle axe at real scale, around 1.2 meters, standing upright on an ice-crystal plinth with its spiked butt resting on the base so it touches the floor as required.

Writing geometry for the haft, plinth, and blade...

Still plotting axe head coordinates...

I'll keep smoothing off to avoid self-intersections, set thickness and bevel values, then paint the blade with a gradient from pale cyan at the edge to deeper blue near the haft, adding a bright white edge line and rune cuts.

Still working out the geometry...

Now I'm planning the head poll block, collars, and top spike proportions relative to the haft, settling on an overall height around 1.52 with the blade centered near y=1.05. For the haft material I'm going with a dark navy steel-ice wood grain texture.

Still working out the grip details: alternating leather wrap rings along the handle using small torus shapes, plus the butt end with a steel cap and spike sinking into an octagonal stone-blue plinth base.

I'm scattering pale cyan ice crystal shards and a few glowing ones around the base, adding icicles under the blade and frost shards near the poll, then placing a glowing octahedron gem on the head front for a cyan-glow, steel, and gold color scheme.

Now I'm finalizing the full palette—steel, gold, ice tones, deep blue, glow cyan, leather, dark wood, and plinth colors—keeping it under 64 for the sprite. For the rune engravings, I'm sketching a tall thin SVG with cyan chevron strokes, then positioning several rune planes along the blade face in world space, spaced out near the upper portion of the blade.

I'm also working out decorative details: separate rune texture variants, placing the planes just off the blade's front face to avoid z-fighting, and considering a gold trim rod running along the blade's inner edge near the haft to add a bit of ornamental flair.

Setting up a joint helper tied to the root bone, then arranging a ring of eight crystals around the plinth, each tilted outward along its radial angle.

Skipping tassels and ribbons for simplicity. I'm setting up the plinth as a two-tier base shape and defining the haft as a hexagonal wooden rod running upward.

Working through blade shading with cel-shaded paint colors and bevel extrusion details, then figuring out the socket box dimensions for the axe head using steel-toned cel paint across the major parts.

Now I'm placing the gold collars and poll details along the haft, sizing the top spike cone to cap the shaft at the right height, positioning the glowing octahedron gem with its bezel ring, and scattering small rivet spheres across the block corners.

Switching the grip to a solid leather-wrapped cylinder with diagonal paint stripes and gold end caps instead of separate rings, then sketching an SVG rune glyph with glowing cyan strokes to texture the haft.

Planning a second diamond-shaped rune variant, glowing both via the glow helper, and setting back-facing planes pointing along negative Z. For the final export I need to carefully track which imports are actually used—THREE, builder, rng, paint, stripes, svg, cel, and glow—to avoid unused-import errors, then add a gold trim rod along the blade's top edge using a polyline through the bone root.

Writing blade paint logic and outline shaping...

I'll keep smoothing at 0 to avoid crossing edges and finalize the polygon with these points.
